avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive antiplatelet effects; increased bleeding risk when combined with NSAID-induced platelet inhibition
avoid_supplements.action: Advise patient to limit vitamin E supplementation to <400 IU/day or discontinue if concurrent use necessary; monitor for signs of bleeding

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic (concentrated supplements)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates antiplatelet and anticoagulant effects; increases GI bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Recommend avoiding concentrated garlic supplements; dietary garlic is acceptable

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Platelet inhibition combined with NSAID effect increases bleeding risk, particularly GI bleeding
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue ginkgo biloba or use with close clinical monitoring; counsel on bleeding signs

caution_supplements.name: Ibuprofen or other NSAIDs (herbal or OTC)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Duplicate NSAID therapy increases GI ulceration, renal dysfunction, and cardiovascular risk
caution_supplements.action: Counsel patient to avoid concurrent NSAIDs; clarify celecoxib is sole NSAID being used

caution_supplements.name: Licorice root
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mineralocorticoid effects promote sodium retention and hypertension; compounds celecoxib's cardiovascular risk
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure; recommend limiting licorice root use to short-term or discontinue if hypertension present

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (high-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet effects; additive with celecoxib's minor antiplatelet properties
caution_supplements.action: Standard dietary omega-3 intake is safe; monitor if using high-dose supplements (>3g/day) with bleeding concerns

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin (high-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet and anticoagulant effects; potential additive GI irritation
caution_supplements.action: Dietary use acceptable; high-dose supplements require monitoring; counsel on GI symptoms

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol (regular/heavy use)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Increases GI bleeding risk; alcohol enhances NSAID-induced gastric mucosal damage and increases cardiovascular and renal toxicity
avoid_foods.action: Advise patient to minimize or eliminate alcohol consumption; warn of increased GI ulceration and bleeding risk

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay celecoxib absorption and increase GI side effects; does not significantly alter bioavailability
caution_foods.action: Take celecoxib with or without food; if GI upset occurs, take with light meal or milk; avoid heavy/fatty foods at time of dosing

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may modestly increase celecoxib levels, though clinical significance is minimal
caution_foods.action: Occasional grapefruit juice consumption is unlikely to cause problems; counsel to limit if concerned

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing foods/beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase GI irritation and acid secretion; minor additive effect with NSAID gastric effects
caution_foods.action: Moderate caffeine intake; if GI symptoms develop, reduce caffeine consumption

monitoring_notes: Assess renal function, blood pressure, and cardiovascular history prior to celecoxib initiation. Monitor for GI symptoms, fluid retention, hypertension, and bleeding signs, particularly in patients combining celecoxib with anticoagulants, antiplatelets, or the supplements listed above.
